fixes.explanation: Verse 7 says, “The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge…” That's the starting line, baker, before any single proverb gets going. Knowledge begins right there. You've got a solid first layer now.

Yes, it's all in one verse. Right after naming where knowledge begins, verse 7 goes on, “…but fools despise wisdom and discipline.” The word but sets the two sides by side. The beginning of knowledge on one side, and what fools despise on the other. Short verse, big contrast.

It really is there, baker. Verse 7 doesn't stop after the fear of the LORD. It keeps going: “…but fools despise wisdom and discipline.” Same verse, same breath. It's an easy one to miss, and I'd double check too.

Verse 8 says, “Listen, my son, to your father’s instruction, and do not forsake the teaching of your mother.” So the father's instruction and the mother's teaching are both named in the same verse. The son is told to listen to the one and not forsake the other.

Verse 11 has the sinners saying, “…let us ambush the innocent without cause…” The people they're after have done nothing to deserve it. I think this one hurts to read. The sinners say it right out loud in their pitch.

The sinners don't claim that, friend. Verse 11 has them say, “…let us ambush the innocent without cause…” So the people they target are innocent, and they plan it without cause. I think this is a heavy line.

In verse 13 the sinners say, “We will find all manner of precious goods; we will fill our houses with plunder.” Notice it's a pitch, baker. Right alongside the goods, they talk about lying in wait for blood in verse 11. Plunder is the prize they're offering.
Peace is a nice thing to promise, but it's not in this pitch. Verse 13 has the sinners say, “we will fill our houses with plunder.” Plunder is what they're selling. Peace never comes up.

That's the twist, baker. Verse 18 says, “But they lie in wait for their own blood; they ambush their own lives.” Back in verse 17 comes the line about spreading the net where any bird can see it. Then verse 18 says the sinners are lying in wait for their own blood. The ambush they talked about is aimed at their own lives.

Verse 19 says, “Such is the fate of all who are greedy, whose unjust gain takes the lives of its possessors.” Remember the plunder and the shared purse from their pitch? The verse says the fate belongs to all who are greedy. Their unjust gain takes the lives of those who hold it.
